test_title: SSC GD Constable (2022) Official Paper (Held On : 12 Jan 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. 

I still enjoyed the week __despite of the weather__.
solution:
The correct answer is **"despite the weather".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is **"I still enjoyed the week despite of the weather."** Here, the phrase **"despite of the weather" **is incorrect because **"despite" **is a preposition that is used **without "of" **when it comes before a noun or a noun phrase.
 
• So, the correct usage is **"despite the weather," **as in **"I still enjoyed the week despite the weather."**

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 4".**​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"Despite"** and **"in spite of" **are two prepositions which are used interchangeably. Both of these expressions can be followed by a noun or a noun phrase.

 
 
• **Example: **"We enjoyed our picnic **despite **the rain."

 
 
• OR "We enjoyed our picnic in spite of the rain."
 
 
 
 
 
• However, neither** "despite"** nor **"in spite of" **are typically followed by **"of". **This is sometimes confused due to the expression **"in spite of" **which does use **"of" **as a part of the phrase.
